title: Old Catholic Archbishop of Utrecht
notes: Elected 15 February 2020 and consecrated 18 September 2021 as the 84th Old Catholic Archbishop of Utrecht; ex officio president of the Union of Utrecht's International Old Catholic Bishops' Conference. Married with four children; spouse name not published.

notes: In office since 10 March 2010; current as of September 2026 (official biography, office since 2010-present; phone call with Coptic Pope, 10 Feb 2026; delegation meetings, May 2026).

title: Grand Mufti of Saudi Arabia
notes: Appointed 22 October 2025 by royal decree of King Salman, succeeding Abdulaziz bin Abdullah Al al-Sheikh, who died 23 September 2025 after 25 years in office; the first Grand Mufti not from the Al al-Sheikh family. Variant spellings: Salih al-Fawzan, Saleh bin Fawzan al-Fawzan. Official office contact details not published; listed site is the scholar's official site.

office_address: Üniversiteler Mah. Dumlupınar Blv. No: 147/A, 06800 Çankaya, Ankara, Türkiye
notes: Appointed 18 September 2025 by presidential decree, succeeding Ali Erbaş (in office 2017-2025); in office September 2026 (2026 Ramadan theme and Hajj programs issued under his name).

title: Grand Mufti of Jerusalem and the Palestinian Territories
notes: Appointed by Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas in 2006; still in office as of September 2026 (fatwa announcements, Jan 2026; detention in July 2026 condemned by Turkish foreign ministry). Office publishes no contact details; no verified official website found.

leader_name: Sheikh Dr. Mohammed bin Abdulkarim Al-Issa
title: Secretary-General of the Muslim World League
office_address: Muslim World League, Old Jeddah Road, Makkah, Al Aqaba District, SA 24312, Saudi Arabia
notes: In office since 2016; current as of September 2026 (MWL activities, August-September 2026). Religious-diplomatic office; the Muslim World League is an international Islamic NGO.

title: President of Religious Affairs at the Grand Mosque and the Prophet's Mosque
notes: President of the Two Holy Mosques affairs since 2012 (re-appointed 2016 and 2020); after the 2023 restructuring he heads the Presidency of Religious Affairs of the Grand Mosque and the Prophet's Mosque; current as of 2026 (Ramadan 1447/2026 operational plan; SPA, July 2026). Office contact details not published; no verified official portal found.

title: Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic of Iran (Velayat-e Faqih)
notes: Succeeded his father Ali Khamenei, killed in a US-Israeli airstrike on 28 February 2026; selected by the Assembly of Experts on 8 March 2026 under wartime conditions, with the IRGC reported by Reuters as having driven the choice; simultaneously elevated from Hojjatoleslam to Ayatollah without official explanation. The succession, and the son-succeeds-father optics, were reported as politically and clerically contested; recorded here only as the holder of the religious office as of September 2026.

title: Grand Ayatollah; Dean of the Hawza of Najaf
notes: Senior living marja'; marja'iyyah since 1993; office active in 2026 (announcements, January and April 2026). Reports note no public appearance since October 2025; the office continues to function.

title: Grand Ayatollah (Marja' al-Taqlid)
notes: Senior marja' of Najaf (b. 1942); active September 2026 (meetings reported August-September 2026).

title: Grand Ayatollah; Head of the Qom Seminary (Hawza Ilmiyya)
notes: Senior Qom marja' (b. 1921); regarded by some scholars as the most learned living Shia authority; current 2026.

title: Grand Ayatollah (Marja' al-Taqlid)
notes: Senior Qom marja' (b. 1927); active 2026 (Hajj statement, July 2026).

title: Grand Ayatollah (Marja' al-Taqlid)
notes: Senior Qom marja' (b. 1925); active 2026 (memorial ceremonies, July 2026).

title: Aga Khan V; 50th hereditary Imam of the Shia Ismaili Muslims
notes: Succeeded his father Prince Karim Aga Khan IV (died 4 February 2025) by nass (designation) in his father's will; announced 5 February 2025 at the Ismaili Centre, Lisbon; succession uncontested. Divorced from Princess Salwa (formerly Kendra Spears); two sons.

title: 53rd al-Dai al-Mutlaq of the Dawoodi Bohra community
notes: In office since 2014 (appointed by his father Mohammed Burhanuddin II); succession was challenged in court by Taher Fakhruddin; the Bombay High Court dismissed the challenge in April 2024, confirming him as Dai al-Mutlaq. Current as of 2026.

title: Khalifatul Masih V (Fifth Caliph of the Messiah)
office_address: Mubarak Mosque, Islamabad, Tilford, Surrey, United Kingdom
notes: Elected 22 April 2003; supreme head of the worldwide Ahmadiyya Muslim Community; current as of 2026 (weekly sermons, September 2026). Mainstream Islam does not recognize the Ahmadiyya movement as Muslim; it is included here as a distinct religious leadership office.

title: Jagadguru Shankaracharya, 36th Peethadheeshwara of Sringeri Sharada Peetham
notes: First of the four cardinal peethams. The official site identifies him as the 36th Peethadheeshwara; successor-designate is Sri Sri Vidhushekhara Bharati Swamiji. Both observed Chaturmasya 29 July-26 September 2026, confirming current tenure. Celibate monastic office. Hinduism has no single head; each Shankaracharya leads only his own peetham.

title: Shankaracharya of Govardhana Math, Puri
notes: Full styling on the matha's official page: 'Swami Sri Nischalananda Saraswati-ji Maharaj'. The official biography states he was appointed head on 9 February 1992; a July 2026 report confirms him in office. Celibate monastic office.

title: Shankaracharya of Dwarka Sharada Peetham
notes: Succeeded Swami Swaroopanand Saraswati (d. 11 September 2022); anointed at Paramhansi Ganga Ashram, Narsinghpur, September 2022 per PTI; active and issuing statements as Shankaracharya through 2026. Name also rendered 'Sadananda Saraswati'. Celibate monastic office. Official website left blank: the peetham's previously listed site could not be verified and directory listings conflict.

title: Claimant to Shankaracharya of Jyotirmath - succession disputed
notes: Declared successor by followers after Swami Swaroopanand Saraswati's death (11 September 2022) per PTI, September 2022. Rival claim by Swami Vasudevanand Saraswati. The Supreme Court's order of 14 October 2022 restrained any coronation pending Civil Appeals 3010/2020 and 3011/2020; the Prayagraj administration issued notices in 2025-26 questioning his claim. Listed here as a disputed claimant, not an undisputed incumbent. Celibate monastic office.

title: Present Spiritual Guru, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha
notes: Sixth and present spiritual guru in the BAPS guru parampara (monastic name Swami Keshavjivandasji), per BAPS official materials. Celibate monastic office.

title: President, Ramakrishna Math and Ramakrishna Mission (17th President)
notes: Full styling: 'Srimat Swami Gautamanandaji Maharaj'. Elected 17th President on 24 April 2024 per Belur Math; presiding at official events through July 2026. Celibate monastic office.

title: Global Head, Chinmaya Mission
notes: Global Head since January 2017; identified as such in an official Chinmaya Mission report of 19 March 2026. Celibate monastic office.

title: 14th Dalai Lama
notes: Spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism, in exile at Dharamshala, India. The official site listed him as scheduled for and attending a Long Life Offering Ceremony in Leh on 30 August 2026, confirming current status. Celibate monastic office.

title: 17th Gyalwa Karmapa - claimant (recognition disputed)
notes: Recognized by Tai Situ Rinpoche and Goshir Gyaltsab Rinpoche, confirmed by the 14th Dalai Lama (official letter, 30 June 1992), enthroned at Tsurphu Monastery 27 September 1992. Rival claimant: Trinley Thaye Dorje (recognized by Shamar Rinpoche, enthroned 17 March 1994). Both claimants signed a joint statement acknowledging past divisions and pledging joint work to preserve the Karma Kagyu lineage. Celibate monastic office.

title: 17th Gyalwa Karmapa - claimant (recognition disputed)
notes: Recognized by Shamar Rinpoche; enthroned 17 March 1994; named legal and administrative successor of the 16th Karmapa by the Karmapa Charitable Trust (17 May 2006); headquarters at Kalimpong, India. Married Rinchen Yangzom (announced 29 March 2017); he no longer performs ordinations. Co-signatory with Ogyen Trinley Dorje of the joint statement on preserving the Karma Kagyu lineage.

title: 20th Supreme Patriarch of Thailand (Sangharaja)
notes: Appointed by King Vajiralongkorn; in office since February 2017; the term is for life. Heads both Thai Theravada fraternities (Maha Nikaya and Dhammayuttika Nikaya) and presides over the Sangha Supreme Council; also abbot of Wat Ratchabophit, Bangkok. The Sangha Supreme Council acknowledged preparations for his 99th birthday in 2026, confirming current tenure. Celibate monastic office.

title: Mahanayake Thera (Chief Prelate), Malwatta Chapter of the Siyam Nikaya
notes: 26th Mahanayake Thera of the Malwatta Chapter; elevated 20 June 2004 by the Karaka Sanga Sabha; based at Malwatta Maha Viharaya, Kandy. A Sri Lankan government programme of 16 April 2026 refers to the incumbent chief prelates of the two chapters. Celibate monastic office.

title: Mahanayaka Thera (Chief Prelate), Asgiriya Chapter of the Siyam Nikaya
notes: 22nd Mahanayake Thera of the Asgiriya Chapter since 7 April 2016; also Chancellor of the Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka. Identified as the incumbent chief prelate in 2026 reporting. Celibate monastic office.

tradition_branch: Myanmar Sangha (State Sangha Maha Nayaka Committee)
title: Chairman, State Sangha Maha Nayaka Committee (Thanlyin Min Kyaung Sayadaw)
notes: Thanlyin Min Kyaung Sayadaw. Identified as chairman of the State Sangha Maha Nayaka Committee in state media reports of February and July 2026. Celibate monastic office.

title: 43rd Sakya Trizin (holder of the Sakya throne)
notes: The throne passed from his elder brother Ratna Vajra (42nd Sakya Trizin) to him on 16 March 2022; he resides at the Sakya Dolma Phodrang, Rajpur, India. The Sakya throne is hereditary in the Khon family and the Trizin may marry: he married Her Eminence Dagmo Sonam Palkyi (also called Dagmo Kushok) on 24 February 2008, per the office's official site.

title: 105th Ganden Tripa, spiritual head of the Gelug school
notes: Formerly Sharpa Choeje Rinpoche; given the responsibility of 105th Ganden Tripa by the 14th Dalai Lama on 2 November 2024 and enthroned at Gaden Lachi on 26 November 2024. The Ganden Tripa is an appointed, seven-year, merit-based office (not a tulku lineage). Celibate monastic office. The 104th Ganden Tripa, Lobsang Tenzin Pelsangpo, died 26 September 2025.

title: Acting Jathedar of the Akal Takht; Jathedar of Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib
notes: Appointed by the SGPC on 7 March 2025 after the removal of Giani Raghbir Singh; assumed charge 10 March 2025; as acting Jathedar he released the Nanakshahi calendar for Sammat 558 (2026-27). Surname also rendered 'Gadgaj'/'Garhgaj'. A rival line named by the 2015 Sarbat Khalsa (Jagtar Singh Hawara / acting Dhian Singh Mand) is not recognized by the SGPC.

title: Acharya, head of the Shwetambar Terapanth
notes: Styled 'Acharyashri Mahashraman' on the order's official site, which identifies him as the current head of the Shwetambar Terapanth organization; active through September 2026. Celibate monastic office.

leader_name: Acharya Samaysagar (Niryapak Muni Samaysagar Ji Maharaj)
title: Acharya, head of the Digambara Vidyasagar sangh
notes: Designated successor of Acharya Vidyasagar (d. 18 February 2024) on 6 February 2024, with formal investiture reported as scheduled for 16 April 2024 at Kundalpur before an assembly of about 400 munis and aryikas. Digambara Jainism has no single universal head; this row covers the Vidyasagar sangh, the largest Digambara order. Celibate monastic office.

title: Sochō (President / Secretary-General), Jinja Honcho
notes: Chief executive and representative officer of the association of about 80,000 shrines. Above the Sochō stand the largely ceremonial Sosai (the head priestess of Ise Grand Shrine) and the Tōri (Takatsukasa Naotake, since 2018). Tanaka's tenure was disputed 2022-2024 after the Tōri nominated a rival, Ashihara Takao; Tanaka's fifth term was confirmed by the Tōri's nomination on 12 December 2024.

title: President (会长), Chinese Taoist Association
office_address: 中华人民共和国北京市西城区白云观街9号白云观
notes: Also known as Li Chengdao (李诚道). President since June 2015; re-elected for the 11th council in December 2025. Also chairman of the World Federation of Taoism (founded September 2023). The Zhengyi Celestial Master (Tianshi) lineage is excluded: after the 64th Celestial Master Zhang Yuanxian died in 2008, multiple rival claimants to the 65th title exist in mainland China and Taiwan, with no universally recognized incumbent.

title: Ashkenazi Chief Rabbi of Israel; President of the Chief Rabbinate Council
notes: Elected in the 2024 Chief Rabbinate elections (first round 29 Sept 2024, second round 31 Oct 2024); took office 4 November 2024 for a 10-year term. Office address, phone and email quoted character-for-character from the Chief Rabbinate's official letterhead (2 July 2026). Official Hebrew honorific used by the office: שליט"א (shlita). Cross-checked against the Chief Rabbinate election record. Judaism has no single world head; the Chief Rabbinate is Israel's state religious authority.

title: Sephardi Chief Rabbi of Israel (Rishon LeZion); President of the Supreme Rabbinical Court
notes: Elected 29 September 2024; took office 4 November 2024 for a 10-year term (Rishon LeZion, 43rd holder of the title). Office address, phone and email quoted from the Chief Rabbinate's official letterhead (2 July 2026). Official Hebrew honorific: שליט"א (shlita). Cross-checked against the Chief Rabbinate election record. Judaism has no single world head.

leader_name: Chief Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis KBE
title: Chief Rabbi of the United Hebrew Congregations of the Commonwealth
office_address: Office of the Chief Rabbi, 305 Ballards Lane, London, N12 8GB, UK
notes: Installed 1 September 2013; 11th Chief Rabbi of the United Hebrew Congregations of the Commonwealth. Knighted 2023 (KBE). Office address, phone and email from the official site's contact page (crawled Sept 2026). Spouse Valerie Mirvis per the official biography.

title: Chief Rabbi of France (Grand Rabbin de France)
notes: Elected 22 June 2014 by the Central Consistory of France (Consistoire central israélite de France); re-elected 6 June 2021 for a seven-year term (through 2028). Confirmed in office by Le Monde, May 2026. Included as one other major national chief rabbi with a clear, verifiable office. Official consistoire website not captured verbatim in sources checked; no published office contact details found.

title: Supreme governing council of the Bahá'í Faith (nine-member collective body)
office_address: Bahá'í World Centre, P.O. Box 155, 3100101 Haifa, Israel
notes: Collective body, not an individual: nine members elected every five years by the members of the world's National Spiritual Assemblies; seated at the Bahá'í World Centre on Mt. Carmel, Haifa. Individual members' names are not officially published on bahai.org — the body acts and signs only as a collective, so no names are listed here. Address, phone and email quoted from official Universal House of Justice correspondence (message of 1 December 2025).

title: Mir of the Yazidis; head of the Supreme Yazidi Spiritual Council
notes: Hereditary Mir since 2019 (succeeded Mir Tahsin Beg, d. 2019). The Mir presides over the Supreme Yazidi Spiritual Council (headquartered at Lalish) and is the highest political and religious authority of the Yazidi community worldwide; the Mir appoints the Baba Sheikh. Address form 'His Excellency / Your Excellency' used by the Presidency of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (Aug 2025). No official published office address, phone or email found.

title: Baba Sheikh (Extiyarê Mergehê) — head of the Yazidi clergy
notes: Appointed Baba Sheikh in November 2020 (confirmed in a statement by KRG Prime Minister Masrour Barzani); succeeded the late Baba Sheikh Khurto Hajji Ismail (d. October 2020) — the succession around 2020 is thus confirmed. Variant spellings in official sources: Ali Elias / Ali Sheikh Alyas. Cross-checked as current in 2026 coverage. No official published office address, phone or email found.

title: Vada Dasturji (High Priest) of the Iranshah Atash Behram, Udvada
notes: One of two serving high priests of the Iranshah Atash Behram at Udvada, Gujarat — the most sacred Parsi fire temple, housing the sacred fire brought from Sanjan. Zoroastrianism has NO single world head; the Udvada high-priestly office is the most senior priestly office of the Indian Parsi community but is not a world head. Confirmed as Udvada High Priest in a 2026 community petition; also documented as high priest of Udvada in 2018 press coverage. No published office contact details found.

title: Vada Dasturji (High Priest) of the Iranshah Atash Behram, Udvada
notes: One of two serving high priests of the Iranshah Atash Behram at Udvada, Gujarat. Zoroastrianism has NO single world head; included only as the highest-profile high-priestly office, which is shared between two concurrent Vada Dasturjis (Dastoor and Mirza). Named as Udvada High Priest in a 2026 community petition. No published office contact details found.

title: Sheikh al-Aql of the Druze Community in Lebanon
notes: Elected in 2021 as Sheikh al-Aql (Sheikh Akl) of the Lebanese Druze community; received as Sheikh Akl by Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri (Lebanese official news agency NNA, 2026). The Druze have NO single world head — Lebanon, Israel and Syria each have their own senior religious leadership. No published office contact details found.

title: Spiritual Leader of the Druze Community in Israel
notes: Spiritual leader of Israel's Druze since 1993 (succeeded his grandfather Amin Tarif). Active in office as of January 2026 (led delegation visiting Syrian Druze patients at Rambam). The Druze have NO single world head. No published office contact details found.

title: Sheikh al-Aql of the Druze of Suwayda, Syria
notes: One of three Sheikh al-Aql in Syria and the most politically prominent as of September 2026. Caveat: Syrian Druze religious leadership is fragmented and contested amid the ongoing conflict; included with this factual caveat. The Druze have NO single world head. No published office contact details found.

title: Shinbashira of Tenrikyo
notes: Fourth Shinbashira, in office since 1998. Per the Constitution of Tenrikyo the Shinbashira is the administrative and spiritual leader who governs Tenrikyo (Tenrikyo Church Headquarters, Tenri, Nara, Japan). Tenrikyo's own English publications use no personal honorific - the office is styled 'the Shinbashira'; salutation left blank on that basis. Spouse Harue Nakayama per official Tenrikyo Online. Currency confirmed via the official Tenrikyo Online New Year's address.
